accreditation.value: Accredited by the Accreditation Board for Specialty Nursing Certification (ABSNC).

year_launched.note: ANCC does not publish a specific launch year for the Cardiac-Vascular Nursing credential on the certification page. Earlier ANCC labeling used RN-BC for this specialty; the credential was standardized under the CV-BC label. Set to null rather than guess.

eligibility.value: Hold a current, active RN license in a US state or territory (or the legally recognized equivalent in another country); have practiced the equivalent of 2 years full-time as a registered nurse; have a minimum of 2,000 hours of clinical practice in cardiac-vascular nursing within the last 3 years; have completed 30 hours of continuing education in cardiac-vascular nursing within the last 3 years.

exam_format.value: Computer-based test at Prometric centers; 150 questions (125 scored + 25 unscored pretest); 3-hour time limit; available year-round during a 120-day testing window after eligibility approval.

passing_score.value: Scaled score of 350 on a 0–500 scale (ANCC standard scaled passing score for board certifications).
passing_score.note: ANCC uses a uniform scaled passing score of 350 across its board certifications per the ANCC Certification Handbook.

retest_fee.note: The specific CV-BC retest fee is not listed on the credential page. Not citing without primary-source confirmation.

pass_rate_2025.note: First-time test takers, 2025 ANCC Certification Data. Listed as 'Cardiac-Vascular Nursing' under RN Specialty Nursing.

renewal_ce_hours.value: 75 contact hours of continuing education in cardiac-vascular nursing; at least 60 of the 75 must be formally approved CE (e.g., ANCC-accredited or AMA PRA Category 1).

renewal_pd_categories.value: In addition to 75 CE hours, complete at least 1 of 8 professional development categories: academic credits, presentations/lectures, publications/research, preceptorship of students, professional service, practice hours (1,000+ in specialty within renewal cycle), quality improvement projects, or re-examination.

salary_context.value: BLS OEWS May 2024 — Registered Nurses (29-1141) mean annual wage approximately $94,480; range roughly $63,720 (10th pctl) to $132,680 (90th pctl). Cardiac-vascular RNs working in cath labs, CTICU/CVICU, electrophysiology, and structural-heart programs often earn above the RN mean.

tco_effective_date.note: Current Test Content Outline took effect 2025-12-05, built from the 2023-2024 Cardiac-Vascular Nursing Role Delineation Study (267 ANCC-certified CV-BC respondents).

blueprint.subtopics: Anatomy and physiology; pathophysiology; nursing diagnosis identification; patient interview (history, chief complaint, social determinants of health); cardiac-vascular assessment techniques and tools (Doppler, stroke scale); data collection and interpretation (diagnostic tests, laboratory results, cardiac rhythms).

Evidence-based practice guidelines (ACC/AHA guidelines, quality measures); scope and standards of practice; legal and ethical considerations (informed consent, advance directives); invasive/non-invasive procedures (peripheral, cardiac, structural); surgeries (coronary/vascular bypass, transplant); pharmacologic therapies; non-pharmacologic and complementary therapies; risk-reduction measures (VTE prophylaxis, infection prevention); prioritization and care coordination (interdisciplinary teams, discharge planning); interventions (targeted temperature management, cardioversion).

Expected outcomes; drug interactions (drug-drug, drug-food); recognition and treatment of adverse reactions and events (heparin-induced thrombocytopenia, hypotension); recognition and treatment of urgent conditions (pseudoaneurysm, hypertensive crisis); recognition and treatment of emergent conditions (pulmonary emboli, stroke).

Cardiac-vascular risk factors (ethnicity, smoking); chronic disease management; cardiac-vascular education topics (procedures, medications); self-management strategies (daily weights, blood pressure logs); community resources (cardiac rehabilitation, anticoagulation clinic); individualized education planning and implementation (addressing barriers, health literacy); outpatient monitoring (remote telemetry, point-of-care testing); health promotion (wellness counseling, health fairs).

common_confusions.scope: Critical-care RN certification for acutely/critically ill patients across ICUs (including CTICU and CVICU). Broader scope than CV-BC; CCRN-certified nurses may also pursue CCRN sub-specialty add-ons for cardiac medicine and cardiac surgery.
Sub-specialty add-on credential for CCRN/PCCN/ACCNS holders who care for acutely ill cardiac-medicine patients (not surgical). Different scope and prerequisite than CV-BC.
Sub-specialty add-on credential for CCRN/PCCN/ACCNS holders who care for adult cardiac-surgery patients in the first 48 hours post-op. Different scope than CV-BC.
Certification for RNs caring for acutely ill adult patients on telemetry, step-down, and intermediate-care units. Overlaps with CV-BC scope but is broader and is not cardiac-specific.

common_confusions.credential: Certified Vascular Nurse (CVN, ANCC renewal only)
common_confusions.scope: Legacy ANCC Certified Vascular Nurse credential; ANCC retired initial testing for this specialty (renewal only). Distinct from CV-BC, which covers cardiac AND vascular nursing under one credential.

discrepancies.resolution: Match. certs.js entry of 150 questions agrees with ANCC primary source (Test Content Outline effective 2025-12-05 and CV-BC credential page). No reconciliation needed.

recent_changes.note: Current 4-domain blueprint (Assessment & Diagnosis 22%, Planning & Implementation 35%, Evaluation & Modification 18%, Patient & Community Education 25%) was issued from the 2023-2024 Cardiac-Vascular Nursing Role Delineation Study (267 ANCC-certified CV-BC respondents).

recent_changes.change: ANCC Certification Renewal Handbook effective September 10, 2025
recent_changes.note: 75 CE hours within the 5-year cycle, with 60 of those formally approved, plus one of eight professional-development categories.
